title: Story of Two GPUs: Characterizing the Resilience of Hopper H100 and Ampere A100 GPUs
problem: Large-scale AI systems with thousands of GPUs require understanding of resilience differences between GPU generations. Memory errors and hardware failures significantly impact job completion and availability.
motivation: Delta supercomputer (1,056 A100 and H100 GPUs, >1.3 exaflops) provides unique opportunity to characterize resilience across large scale over extended operational period (2.5 years, 11.7M GPU hours).
method: Analysis of 2.5 years operational error data from Delta system. Comparison of memory error rates (MTBE), hardware resilience across critical components, and failure mechanisms. Projection of GPU node availability impact at larger scales.
key_novelty: First comprehensive empirical comparison of H100 vs. A100 GPU resilience at exascale; quantification of memory error degradation in H100; identification of recovery mechanism insufficiencies; large-scale failure mode analysis.
contributions: H100 GPU memory resilience 3.2x worse than A100 (lower per-GPU MTBE)
H100 memory error-recovery mechanisms insufficient for increased memory capacity
H100 demonstrates improved hardware resilience over A100 for critical components
GPU errors frequently result in job failures due to lack of robust application-level recovery
Projection of 5% GPU overprovisioning necessary to handle failures at larger scales
limitations: Delta-specific results; limited to Ampere and Hopper; memory vs. compute error distribution not detailed; application-level recovery mechanisms not proposed
primary_theme: GPU Generation Resilience Comparison at Exascale
